feat(agent): calibrate needs-reply score to an empirical probability (v0.2.0b88)

The classifier's score is an additive heuristic — 0.85 does NOT mean 85% likely
to deserve a reply. Calibration learns, from the user's own past verdicts, what
fraction of messages at each score level actually deserved a reply, and maps a
raw score to that empirical probability — the principled gate an act decision
can eventually tie to a precision target.

backend admission / prompt prefill before emitting its first SSE event. The

reports). The OpenAI SDK's own streaming read timeout is 600s, so 12s was
~50x more aggressive than the transport layer would have tolerated.

admitFromQueue enforced limit_per_day by counting approved rows whose
queued_at fell in today's range, but admission never recorded when it
happened — so a backlog queued on a prior day and admitted today counted

[fix] queue: SendMessages signal-fail teardown starved waiting groups

When the steer-into-dying-container race freed the active slot, SendMessages
cleared s.active and decremented activeCount but never drained
waitingGroups — a group parked on the concurrency/folder limit could starve
indefinitely (with maxConcurrent=1, forever). Drain after teardown like
runForGroup does, guarded so a concurrent runForGroup completion can't
double-decrement.

[fix] store: FlushSysMsgs swallowed errors, risked duplicate delivery

FlushSysMsgs ignored rows.Scan/rows.Err and the DELETE/Commit errors, then
returned the rendered body unconditionally. On a commit failure the caller
delivered system messages that were never deleted → re-flushed next time
(duplicates). Check each error and return "" without consuming on any
failure, so undeleted rows are retried rather than double-delivered.

etc.) can deliver terminal focus reports (CSI I / CSI O) to the
running TUI. prompt_toolkit does not map those sequences by default,

inserts `[I` / `[O` into the prompt buffer after the ESC byte is
handled.

[fix] webd: SSE round_done not filtered by turn_id closes wrong stream

Per-turn SSE streams subscribe by (folder, topic). message frames were
filtered by turn_id but round_done was not, so a second turn in the same

with a non-UTC offset ("...+09:00") sorts lexically above a UTC now
("...Z"), so a past-due task is never claimed. Wrap both sides in
SQLite datetime() to normalize offsets to UTC before comparison.
